suite.name: SCG Local-IPC Latency & SHM Honest-Latency Suite
suite.description: Answers 'why is SHM latency so bad / shouldn't it be sub-us?' by measuring the honest closed-loop RTT (mode=pingpong, one message in flight) of the shared-memory, Unix-socket and TCP data paths through one SCG (scg-direct), alongside the sustained-throughput blast p99 for SHM. The RTT rows show SHM's real turnaround is microseconds (comparable to UDS and loopback TCP on this NIC-less host — a socket-like copy-in/out + syscall-per-wakeup, not a NIC-bypass win), while the throughput rows show the multi-millisecond p99 is open-loop queue backlog (coordinated omission), not the transport. This is the RC2/RC4 story made measurable and the F16 SHM/UDS RTT data. Empirical note: the fixed-slot ring (shm_ring_kind=slot) + futex was measured SLOWER for RTT (~55 us vs ~17 us byte-stream) and needs shm_segment_size >= payload for throughput, so the default byte-stream + eventfd config is used here; the slot-ring underperformance is a separate finding. Plaintext routing (protocol none), no certificates.
suite.author: SESHAT

scenarios.name: shmzc_shm_tput_4KB
scenarios.description: SHM sustained throughput through one SCG (byte-stream ring); p99 here is open-loop blast queue backlog, NOT turnaround. 4 KB.

scenarios.name: shmzc_shm_tput_64KB
scenarios.description: SHM sustained throughput through one SCG (byte-stream ring); p99 here is open-loop blast queue backlog, NOT turnaround. 64 KB.

scenarios.name: shmzc_shm_slot_tput_64KB
scenarios.description: SHM sustained throughput, fixed-slot ring sized to the payload (shm_segment_size >= message). Reaches TCP-loopback line rate (~45-47 Gbps) where the default 4 MiB byte-stream ring backpressures to ~30. Routing slot ring, so the gateway relays it with the zero-copy c2g path. 64 KB.

scenarios.name: shmzc_shm_slot_tput_1MB
scenarios.description: SHM sustained throughput, fixed-slot ring, 1 MB messages. Above the 512 KiB threshold the gateway writes each frame straight from shared memory to the upstream (zero-copy c2g direct-write): same throughput at lower gateway CPU vs the staging-copy path (cache-busting payload). 1 MB.

scenarios.name: shmzc_shm_paced_bs_4KB
scenarios.description: SHM paced latency, byte-stream ring: the sender builds each message in a buffer and copies it into the ring via send_msg (baseline for the generator-into-ring comparison). 4 KB @ 2 Gbps offered.

scenarios.name: shmzc_shm_paced_slot_4KB
scenarios.description: SHM paced latency, slot ring: the workload generator stamps each message STRAIGHT INTO the ring slot (reserve + build_into + commit) — zero staging buffer, no buffer->ring copy on the client side. 4 KB @ 2 Gbps offered.

scenarios.name: shmzc_shm_scale_16KB_1c
scenarios.description: SHM slot-ring throughput scaling, 1 connection. Slot geometry is AUTO-SIZED from the message size (only shm_ring_kind=slot given) — no hand-computed segment_size. Baseline for the connection sweep.

scenarios.name: shmzc_shm_scale_16KB_4c
scenarios.description: SHM slot-ring throughput scaling, 4 connections (auto-sized slot ring). Compare to 1c: SHM currently does not scale with connections (a per-message-rate wall, not memory bandwidth) — this row tracks that in the nightly.

scenarios.name: shmzc_shm_scale_16KB_16c
scenarios.description: SHM slot-ring throughput scaling, 16 connections (auto-sized slot ring). Tracks the SHM connection-scaling ceiling in the nightly alongside the 1c/4c rows.
